knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies on a Plane

question.:question/problem:
Determine whether $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi:\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{b}+t\mathbf{c}$, where $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{b}&=\langle -2, -1, -2\rangle \\ \mathbf{c}&=\langle 3, 1, -1\rangle \\ \mathbf{u}&=\langle 2, 2, 10\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

If it does, select the value of $s\cdot t$ in $\mathbf{u}=s\mathbf{b}+t\mathbf{c}$. Otherwise, select the statement that $\mathbf{u}$ does not lie on $\Pi$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{u}\in\Pi$ exactly when the same values of $s$ and $t$ satisfy all three coordinate equations. Expanding the vector equation gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2s+3t &=2 \\ -s+t &=2 \\ -2s-t &=10\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 10\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2 \leftarrow R_2-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)R_1$, then $R_3 \leftarrow R_3-(1)R_1$, then $R_3 \leftarrow R_3-(8)R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row is $0=0$, so it adds no restriction. Back substitute in the two nonzero rows:

$$
\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{1}{-\frac{1}{2}}=-2 \\ s&=\frac{2-(3)(-2)}{-2}=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Verify every coordinate:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4)(-2)+(-2)(3)&=2=2 \\ (-4)(-1)+(-2)(1)&=2=2 \\ (-4)(-2)+(-2)(-1)&=10=10\end{aligned}
$$

All three coordinates agree, so the vector lies on the plane. Therefore,

$$
s\cdot t=(-4)\cdot(-2)=8.
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/feedback: The pair $s=-4,t=-2$ satisfies all three coordinates; the vector lies on the plane.
Correct. The common pair satisfies all three equations and gives $s\cdot t=8$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies on a Plane

question.:question/problem:
Determine whether $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi:\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{b}+t\mathbf{c}$, where $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{b}&=\langle 2, -3, -2\rangle \\ \mathbf{c}&=\langle -2, -3, 3\rangle \\ \mathbf{u}&=\langle 8, -12, -8\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

If it does, select the value of $s\cdot t$ in $\mathbf{u}=s\mathbf{b}+t\mathbf{c}$. Otherwise, select the statement that $\mathbf{u}$ does not lie on $\Pi$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{u}\in\Pi$ exactly when the same values of $s$ and $t$ satisfy all three coordinate equations. Expanding the vector equation gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2s-2t &=8 \\ -3s-3t &=-12 \\ -2s+3t &=-8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -2 & 8 \\ -3 & -3 & -12 \\ -2 & 3 & -8\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2 \leftarrow R_2-\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)R_1$, then $R_3 \leftarrow R_3-(-1)R_1$, then $R_3 \leftarrow R_3-\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right)R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row is $0=0$, so it adds no restriction. Back substitute in the two nonzero rows:

$$
\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{0}{-6}=0 \\ s&=\frac{8-(-2)(0)}{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

Verify every coordinate:

$$
\begin{aligned}(4)(2)+(0)(-2)&=8=8 \\ (4)(-3)+(0)(-3)&=-12=-12 \\ (4)(-2)+(0)(3)&=-8=-8\end{aligned}
$$

All three coordinates agree, so the vector lies on the plane. Therefore,

$$
s\cdot t=(4)\cdot(0)=0.
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/feedback: The pair $s=4,t=0$ satisfies all three coordinates; the vector lies on the plane.
Correct. The common pair satisfies all three equations and gives $s\cdot t=0$.

question.:question/problem:
Determine whether $\mathbf{u}$ lies on the plane $\Pi:\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{b}+t\mathbf{c}$, where $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{b}&=\langle 3, -1, -1\rangle \\ \mathbf{c}&=\langle -2, 1, -1\rangle \\ \mathbf{u}&=\langle 3, 0, -7\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

If it does, select the value of $s\cdot t$ in $\mathbf{u}=s\mathbf{b}+t\mathbf{c}$. Otherwise, select the statement that $\mathbf{u}$ does not lie on $\Pi$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
By definition, $\mathbf{u}\in\Pi$ exactly when the same values of $s$ and $t$ satisfy all three coordinate equations. Expanding the vector equation gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3s-2t &=3 \\ -s+t &=0 \\ -s-t &=-7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -7\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2 \leftarrow R_2-\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)R_1$, then $R_3 \leftarrow R_3-\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)R_1$, then $R_3 \leftarrow R_3-(-5)R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

The last row gives $0=-1$, a contradiction. No pair satisfies all three equations. Thus $\mathbf{u}$ does not lie on $\Pi$. A product obtained from only two coordinates is not a valid answer.
